qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Portfolio of specialized niche industrial leaders (Markem-Imaje coding/ink consumables, OPW fueling/clean energy hardware, PSG biopharma & specialty pumps) benefits from installed-base switching costs and consumable replenishment. However, consolidated capital efficiency fails empirical moat hurdles: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~10.1% (FY21 11.7%, FY22 11.7%, FY23 9.9%, FY24 9.9%, FY25 10.3%), structurally below the 12.0% threshold due to continuous M&A goodwill dilution (~$4.5B+ goodwill) and cyclical competition in commercial refrigeration and engineered components.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). While Dover operates defensible niche positions with switching costs in marking consumables (Markem-Imaje), retail fueling hardware (OPW), and specialty pumps (PSG), its consolidated 5-year median GAAP ROIC of ~10.1% (2021-2025 range of 9.9% to 11.7%) structurally fails the 12% cycle hurdle. Substantial goodwill from continuous bolt-on M&A and cyclical headwinds in climate/engineered goods dilute returns.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~10.1% (FY21 11.7%, FY22 11.7%, FY23 9.9%, FY24 9.9%, FY25 10.3%), consistently below the 12.0% hurdle across economic cycle peaks and normalizations. Consolidated revenue ~$8.1B in FY25 across five segments (Clean Energy & Fueling, Pumps & Process Solutions, Climate & Sustainability, Engineered Products, Imaging & Identification). Operating margins have hovered between 15.6% and 17.0%. FCF generation is healthy (~$1.0B-$1.1B annually, ~13-14% FCF margin), but heavy historical M&A has accumulated over $4.5B in goodwill, preventing capital returns from exceeding cost of capital by an elite compounder margin.
